key_insight: This paper shows that large language models can be guided to propose exact structural edits that make hard-to-synthesize molecules more synthesizable, rather than simply generating new molecules from scratch. The approach improves over traditional methods while helping preserve important molecular features.
problem_solved: Many AI drug-design systems produce molecules with promising properties but poor synthesizability, creating a gap between model output and practical lab feasibility. This work addresses the challenge of repairing such molecules with minimal, targeted changes.
method: Train/guided an LLM to predict a sequence of molecular edits instead of a single final structure.
Use edit-sequence prediction to iteratively transform unsynthesizable molecules into more synthesizable ones.
Optimize for maintaining key molecular features while improving synthesizability, enabling more practical design candidates.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates a more controllable and chemistry-aware generation strategy that bridges model design and experimental usability. It suggests LLMs can be used not just for generation, but for precise molecule refinement in real-world pipelines.
visual_elements: Before/after molecule edit flow showing unsynthesizable to synthesizable transformation

paper_title: Guiding large language models to predict edit sequences for molecular synthesizability optimization
